issues.legal_issue: A landlord may contest an applicant’s tenant status in a renewed proceeding to determine the purchase price, notwithstanding an earlier order declaring the purchase ineffective because the applicant did not appear.
material_facts: The applicant sought a renewed opportunity to purchase land after an earlier proceeding declared the purchase ineffective because he failed to appear.
The landlord was served in the earlier proceeding, and the applicant’s tenant status had not been adjudicated there.
The landlord opposed the renewed application by disputing that the applicant was a tenant on the relevant date.
issues.conclusion: The earlier order and the landlord’s failure to challenge it did not, by themselves, preclude the landlord from disputing the applicant’s tenant status in the renewed proceeding. If the landlord had appeared earlier and unequivocally admitted that status, the landlord would have been estopped from disputing it later.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 32, 32G and 32PP of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, a person seeking the renewed opportunity must establish the relevant tenant status as well as the earlier failure to appear and resulting ineffective purchase. A notice and nonappearance do not amount to an adjudication of tenant status, so neither res judicata nor constructive res judicata bars a later inquiry into that status. An unequivocal admission by the landlord in the earlier proceeding may, however, create an estoppel. Relying on Sri Ram Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay, the Court noted that title passes by operation of law on the tillers’ day, subject to the statutory conditions.

rule.if: renewed_purchase_price_application and prior_purchase_declared_ineffective_for_nonappearance and tenant_status_not_adjudicated_earlier and not landlord_unequivocally_admitted_tenant_status

predicates.renewed_purchase_price_application: A person applies for a renewed opportunity to purchase land and have its purchase price determined.
predicates.prior_purchase_declared_ineffective_for_: An earlier purchase proceeding declared the purchase ineffective because the person failed to appear.
predicates.tenant_status_not_adjudicated_earlier: The earlier proceeding did not decide whether the applicant was a tenant on the relevant date.
predicates.landlord_unequivocally_admitted_tenant_s: The landlord appeared in the earlier proceeding and unequivocally admitted that the defaulting person was a tenant on the relevant date.
predicates.landlord_may_contest_applicant_tenant_st: The landlord is permitted to dispute the applicant’s tenant status in the renewed proceeding.

issues.definition: When a renewed purchase-price application follows an ineffective purchase declaration for nonappearance and tenant status was not previously adjudicated, the landlord may contest that status unless the landlord unequivocally admitted it earlier.

issues.legal_issue: The evidentiary record established the applicant’s tenant status, so the matter did not need to be remitted for a new determination of that status.
material_facts: The applicant’s name appeared in tenancy records for certain years, and notice of the earlier purchase proceeding had been sent to him using the tenancy record.
The landlord did not place on record a statement from the earlier proceeding showing that he disputed the applicant’s status.
The landlord took no step under section 15 after the purchase was declared ineffective.
The landlord did not examine the other person whom he claimed was the land’s only tenant.
issues.conclusion: The cumulative circumstances affirmatively established that the applicant was a tenant on the relevant date. The tribunal was therefore right to direct that the purchase price be determined, and remittal was unnecessary.
issues.legal_principle: In a proceeding under sections 32G and 32PP of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, tenant status on the relevant date is a jurisdictional fact. Although the landlord may contest that status, the Court assessed the cumulative evidence in the record and concluded that it established the applicant’s tenancy. Sri Ram Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay was relied on for the principle that title passes to the tenant by operation of law on the tillers’ day, subject to the statutory conditions.

rule.if: appeal_from_tenant_purchase_price_determination and tenancy_records_identify_applicant and earlier_notice_sent_to_applicant_based_on_tenancy_record and landlord_did_not_record_status_dispute and landlord_took_no_recovery_step_after_ineffective_purchase and landlord_did_not_examine_alternative_claimed_tenant

predicates.appeal_from_tenant_purchase_price_determ: An appeal challenges a determination in a proceeding seeking to have the purchase price fixed after an earlier purchase was declared ineffective.
predicates.tenancy_records_identify_applicant: Tenancy records identify the applicant as a tenant for some period.
predicates.earlier_notice_sent_to_applicant_based_o: Notice of the earlier purchase proceeding was sent to the applicant on the basis of the tenancy record.
predicates.landlord_did_not_record_status_dispute: The landlord did not place on record a statement from the earlier proceeding disputing the applicant’s tenant status.
predicates.landlord_took_no_recovery_step_after_ine: The landlord took no step to recover the land after the purchase was declared ineffective.
predicates.landlord_did_not_examine_alternative_cla: The landlord did not examine the person whom he claimed was the only tenant.
predicates.applicant_tenant_status_established_and_: The applicant’s tenant status is established on the record, and the matter need not be remitted for a new determination.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a purchase-price determination, the stated cumulative circumstances establish the applicant’s tenant status and make remittal unnecessary.
